# Tuesday Design Review - 2026-03-10
## Attendees: Sarah (PM), Mike (Frontend Lead), Priya (Design), Carlos (UX Research), Jennifer (VP Product)

### Agenda: Settings Page & Mobile Strategy

**Priya** presented two design options for the settings page:
- Option A: Tab-based layout (similar to current pattern)
- Option B: Single scrolling page with section anchors (modern approach)

**Carlos** shared user research: 73% of users change settings on mobile. Current tab pattern has 45% abandonment rate on mobile.

**Discussion:**
- Jennifer strongly prefers Option B, says it aligns with the new design system
- Mike raised concern about Option B requiring more frontend refactoring
- Sarah asked about timeline impact - Priya estimates Option B adds 2 days vs Option A

### Decisions
- **Go with Option B** (single scrolling page) per Jennifer's direction
- **Use React for implementation** - wait, Jennifer mentioned we should evaluate Vue.js for new components as the company is considering a framework migration
- Mobile-first approach: design for mobile, then adapt for desktop
- Priya to update Figma by Wednesday noon

### Action Items
- [ ] Priya: Update Figma with Option B, mobile-first, by Wednesday noon
- [ ] Mike: Spike on Option B implementation complexity (2 hours)
- [ ] Carlos: Share full user research report with team by Wednesday
- [ ] Jennifer: Send email about Vue.js evaluation criteria
- [ ] Sarah: Update project timeline to reflect 2-day extension

### Notes
- Jennifer wants a demo of the settings page at next week's exec review
- Carlos will run usability tests on the new design with 5 users next week
- Priya mentioned she's taking PTO March 20-24

# Thursday Stakeholder Sync - 2026-03-12
## Attendees: Sarah (PM), Jennifer (VP Product), David (CTO), Rachel (VP Sales), Mark (CS Lead)

### Agenda: Q2 Roadmap & Current Sprint

**Jennifer** provided product update:
- Settings page on track for demo next week
- Mobile responsive work progressing well
- Considering framework migration to Vue.js (exploratory)

**David (CTO)** raised concerns:
- Angular migration was planned 6 months ago, we committed to it in the technical roadmap
- Vue.js evaluation would need a formal RFC process (minimum 4 weeks)
- Prefers we stick with React for now and evaluate frameworks in Q3
- **New requirement**: All API endpoints must support pagination by end of Q2. This is blocking enterprise customer onboarding.

**Rachel (VP Sales)** shared:
- 3 enterprise deals ($500K total) waiting on pagination support
- Customers also asking for SAML SSO integration (currently only Okta)
- Q2 target: close 10 enterprise deals, need technical features delivered

**Mark (CS Lead)**:
- Current customers reporting slow search - confirms Lisa's finding
- Need bulk export for compliance reporting - already in sprint backlog
- Settings page redesign is top customer request

### Decisions
- **Pagination is now P0** for Q2 - must be in next sprint planning
- **SAML SSO** added to Q2 roadmap (target: end of April)
- **Framework migration deferred** to Q3 evaluation (David's recommendation accepted)
- Settings page demo confirmed for next Thursday's exec review

### Action Items
- [ ] Lisa: Estimate pagination work for all API endpoints by Friday
- [ ] Sarah: Reprioritize Sprint 23 backlog to include pagination spike
- [ ] David: Write technical RFC template for framework evaluation
- [ ] Rachel: Compile list of enterprise feature requirements by Monday
- [ ] Mark: Aggregate customer feedback on search performance
- [ ] Sarah: Schedule SAML SSO planning session for next week

### Impact Assessment
- Pagination work was NOT in Sprint 23 plan
- Adding pagination spike means something else needs to drop
- Sarah notes: Angular migration items in Sprint 23 may conflict with the framework deferral decision

### Open Questions
- If pagination is P0, do we pull Angular migration from Sprint 23?
- Do we need a dedicated sprint for pagination, or can it be incremental?
- Who owns the SAML SSO implementation?

# Friday Retrospective - Sprint 22 Review - 2026-03-13
## Attendees: Sarah (PM), Mike (Frontend Lead), Lisa (Backend Lead), Tom (QA), Priya (Design), Alex (DevOps)

### Sprint 22 Results
- Planned: 95 points
- Completed: 78 points (82% completion)
- Carried over: 17 points (navigation component polish, 2 bug fixes)

### What Went Well
- Navigation component shipped and customers love it (+15 positive feedback tickets)
- Alex's monitoring stack deployment was smooth
- Good collaboration between Mike and Priya on navigation design
- Test coverage improved from 67% to 74%

### What Didn't Go Well
- Lisa's API refactoring took longer than estimated (complexity underestimated)
- Tom was blocked for 2 days waiting on staging access
- Sprint scope creep: 3 unplanned items added mid-sprint
- Design specs delivered late (Thursday instead of Tuesday), cascading delay

### Action Items for Improvement
- [ ] Sarah: Implement stricter scope change process - no additions without removing equal points
- [ ] Alex: Create self-service staging access provisioning (reduce blocker risk)
- [ ] Priya: Commit to delivering specs 1 day before sprint planning
- [ ] Lisa: Break down large refactoring tasks into smaller, independently deliverable chunks
- [ ] Tom: Create staging environment checklist to verify access before sprint starts

### Team Morale
- Overall: 7/10 (down from 8/10 last sprint)
- Concern about growing backlog and shifting priorities
- Mike expressed frustration about Angular migration being planned then potentially cancelled
- Lisa worried about API pagination being added on top of existing sprint commitments

### Process Changes
- Agreed: Design specs must be finalized before sprint planning (not during)
- Agreed: Maximum 2 unplanned items per sprint, with formal trade-off discussion
- Trial: Pair programming sessions for complex features (Lisa + Wei for rate limiting)

### Kudos
- Mike: exceptional work on the navigation component under pressure
- Alex: proactive monitoring stack deployment saved us from a potential outage
- Tom: thoroughness in test coverage improvement

### Notes
- Sprint 23 already planned (see Wednesday notes) but may need revision based on Thursday's new requirements
- Sarah to send out revised sprint plan by Monday morning
- Next retrospective: March 27
